question: What attendance rate must international students at AIS achieve before Immigration New Zealand will accept a student visa renewal application?
gold_answer: Over 95% attendance (together with passing at least 75% of courses) is required before Immigration New Zealand will accept a student visa renewal application via Provider Direct Student (PDS).

question: What percentage of their courses must international students pass for a student visa renewal via Provider Direct Student?
gold_answer: International students must pass at least 75% of their courses.

question: How many credits is the COMP901 Information Technology Research Thesis worth?
gold_answer: COMP901 Information Technology Research Thesis is worth 90 credits at Level 9.

question: What penalty interest rate does AIS charge on overdue fee payments?
gold_answer: Penalty interest of 2.5% per month is charged on any overdue amount from the overdue date until payment in full is received.

question: What is the cross-credit application fee for courses completed overseas?
gold_answer: NZ$275 per course for studies completed overseas (NZ$50 per course for studies completed in New Zealand); fees are non-refundable.

question: What grade is recorded if a student withdraws from a course after the fifth week of the trimester?
gold_answer: A grade of 'E' (Failure to complete) is recorded for withdrawals received after the fifth week of the trimester.

question: What is the maximum number of cross-credits available for the Master of Information Technology?
gold_answer: 90 credits, at Level 8 only.

question: Which body approves cross-credit applications at AIS?
gold_answer: The Board of Studies approves cross-credit applications; the student is then notified of the result by email.

question: What are the minimum device requirements under the AIS Bring Your Own Device policy?
gold_answer: An iOS 13, Android 12 or MS Windows 11 operating system in English, Office 365 compatibility, at least a 10-inch screen, 8GB memory (16GB preferred), Wi-Fi, and mouse, keyboard or touchscreen, webcam, microphone and speakers.

question: Where is AIS student enrolment and qualification completion data stored?
gold_answer: In the Cloud, in a Microsoft datastore based in Sydney, Australia.

question: I want to take the MIT thesis pathway. Which compulsory research course must I complete at Level 8, and how many credits is the thesis itself?
gold_answer: COMP801 Research Methods (15 credits) is the compulsory Level 8 course, and the Level 9 COMP901 Information Technology Research Thesis is 90 credits.

question: If I am caught cheating in an assessment and ultimately expelled, what disciplinary measures apply and will my fees be refunded?
gold_answer: Penalties for plagiarism or cheating include demerit points, removal of marks and direction to repeat courses, escalating to suspension or expulsion; fees are non-refundable if a student is expelled or suspended by AIS.

question: What happens to my enrolment if I stop attending classes during the refund period, and how could poor attendance affect my visa renewal?
gold_answer: A student who stops attending before the end of the refund period is treated as having withdrawn within the refund period. For Immigration New Zealand to accept a student visa renewal application via Provider Direct Student (PDS), the student must achieve over 95% attendance and pass at least 75% of courses.

question: I need to apply for a student visa after paying my fees. What documents will AIS send me for the visa application, and what refund applies if Immigration New Zealand declines my visa?
gold_answer: After payment is processed AIS sends a Receipt and a Confirmation of Enrolment, which must be sent with the Student Visa application; a full refund is given if the student visa is declined by Immigration New Zealand.

question: How are my tuition fees protected before AIS delivers tuition, and what happens to fees if AIS cancels my course?
gold_answer: All fees are held in an independent Chartered Accountant's trust account and released to AIS progressively (the lesser of 20% or $3,000 after the statutory withdrawal period, the rest pro rata in arrears); if AIS cancels a course or qualification, full refunds are given.

question: I completed IT courses overseas and want to cross-credit them to the Master of Information Technology. How many credits can I claim at most, and what does each application cost?
gold_answer: Up to 90 credits (Level 8 only) can be cross-credited towards the MIT. Applications cost NZ$275 per course for studies completed overseas (non-refundable, paid before processing); no fee applies to courses included in an approved articulation agreement.

question: What can happen if AIS discovers I submitted falsified documents, and what does that mean for my fees?
gold_answer: AIS may suspend or terminate enrolment if falsified documents are discovered; fees are non-refundable if a student is expelled or suspended.

question: Which specialist courses are available in the MIT Information Systems topic, and can one of them be replaced with COMP805?
gold_answer: INFO812 Data Mining, INFO813 Artificial Intelligence and INFO814 Enterprise Cloud-based Systems (15 credits each); COMP805 Specialisation Project may be substituted for any specialist course with the approval of the Head of Programme.

question: I am an international student in a 12-month programme and I want to withdraw two weeks before the programme starts. What refund am I entitled to?
gold_answer: Students withdrawing within one month prior to the start of the programme are entitled to a refund less a deduction of 17.5%.

question: I am a domestic student in a programme over three months and withdraw on day 5 after the start. What will be refunded?
gold_answer: All payments exceeding NZ$500 or 10% of the fees paid, whichever is the lesser, are refunded for withdrawals within the first seven days.

question: I withdrew from a course in week 4 of the trimester, three weeks after the programme started. What grade will I receive, and what would it be if I had waited until week 7?
gold_answer: Withdrawal after 14 calendar days and before the end of week 5 incurs a grade of 'WD' (Withdrawn); after the fifth week it incurs a grade of 'E' (Failure to complete).

question: My English programme is 8 weeks long and I withdrew on the third day after it began. How much of my fees will be refunded?
gold_answer: 75% of the fees paid is refunded for programmes of five weeks or more but less than three months when the student withdraws prior to or within the first five days.

question: A student has accumulated three major demerit points. What action can the Student Disciplinary Committee take?
gold_answer: The SDC has the right to suspend or expel a student for an accumulation of three major demerit points.

question: I am entering the Bachelor of Information Technology and have completed a relevant New Zealand Level 5 diploma. What credit can I receive and do I need to pay an application fee?
gold_answer: You may be entitled to advanced standing credit (ASC) for up to 240 credits; no application or fees apply, but ASC must be approved by the Board of Studies.

question: I am enrolled in the Master of Information Technology at AIS. Is my spouse eligible for a work visa under the Family Stream?
gold_answer: Eligibility requires enrolment in a Level 7 or higher qualification in an area of absolute skill shortage on the Long Term Skill Shortage List, or the MBA; the MIT is Level 9, so eligibility depends on whether the study area is on the Long Term Skill Shortage List, and the application must be made directly to Immigration New Zealand.

question: I was granted Permanent Residency halfway through the trimester I have already paid for. Will my international fees be adjusted?
gold_answer: No. Fees are not adjusted if an international student's immigration status changes to Permanent Resident during the enrolment period paid for.

gold_answer: Where the student visa application is declined while studying on an interim visa, fees are charged pro rata for the weeks attended and the balance is refunded.

question: What is the late submission penalty for the COMP901 thesis?

question: Who marks the COMP901 thesis and how is the final mark calculated?

question: How many marks is the data analysis criterion worth in the COMP901 thesis marking scheme?

question: What must I include in my COMP901 thesis if I used AI tools during the research?

question: If I use AI tools in my COMP901 thesis without declaring them, what penalties could I face under AIS rules?
gold_answer: Submissions are checked for copied material and AI use, with penalties applied if not referenced; under AIS disciplinary rules, plagiarism or cheating in assessments can lead to demerit points, removal of marks, direction to repeat courses, and escalate to suspension or expulsion.

question: How many marks is the literature review worth in the COMP901 thesis, and what causes deductions on that criterion?

question: How many credits is COMP901 worth in the MIT programme, and what proportion of the course marks does the thesis assignment carry?

question: What is the discussion chapter worth in the COMP901 thesis marking scheme, and what specifically loses marks there?
gold_answer: The discussion is worth 15 marks; marks are deducted for lack of clarity, lack of relevance to the body or empirical work, and if limitations are not present or not accurate.

question: I submitted my COMP901 thesis two days after the deadline. How much will be deducted from my mark?
gold_answer: 10% of the available marks (5% per 24-hour day, applied for each of the two days late).

question: What happens if I submit my COMP901 thesis five days after the due date?

question: Moodle is down and I cannot submit my COMP901 thesis through it. Can I hand in a printed copy instead?
gold_answer: No. If unable to submit via Moodle, email the submission to your supervisor; only electronic submissions are marked and hard-copy submissions will not be marked.

question: If I upload a draft of my COMP901 thesis a week before the deadline and a revised version on the due date, which version is marked?
gold_answer: Drafts may be resubmitted until the due date; on the due date the latest version is accepted as the final version, so the revised version is marked.

question: As an MIT student, when does Trimester 1 run in 2026, and how long does the whole MIT programme take?

question: Besides IELTS, which other English language qualifications are accepted for entry to the MIT?
gold_answer: Accepted alternatives to IELTS 6.5 academic (no band below 6.0) are TOEFL iBT 79 with a writing score of 21, PToE academic score of 58 with no band lower than 50, and NZCEL (Academic) Level 5.

question: What academic qualifications do I need to be admitted to the Master of Information Technology?
gold_answer: Entry requires a bachelor degree, graduate diploma or postgraduate diploma, or equivalent, in information technology, computer science or a related field of study. Applications outside the stated criteria are assessed case-by-case.

question: What are the 2026 MIT fees for domestic students?
gold_answer: For domestic students the 2026 programme fees are NZ$9,720 plus resource fees of NZ$3,540, a total of NZ$13,260, plus the compulsory Student Services Fee of NZ$300 per year. The programme is eligible for a StudyLink student loan.

question: Which courses make up the Networks and Security specialist topic in the MIT?
gold_answer: The Networks and Security specialist topic comprises CONE809 Topics in Cloud Computing, CONE810 Computer and Communication Network Security, and CONE811 Penetration Testing. Availability of this topic should be verified before enrolment.

question: My TOEFL iBT total is 79 but my writing score is 19. Do I meet the MIT English requirement through TOEFL?
gold_answer: No. The TOEFL iBT pathway requires a total of 79 with a writing score of 21, so a writing score of 19 does not meet the requirement. The student would need a TOEFL iBT result that meets the writing requirement, or another accepted qualification (IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0, PToE 58 with no band lower than 50, or NZCEL (Academic) Level 5).

question: I hold a bachelor degree in marketing. Do I meet the academic entry requirements for the MIT?
gold_answer: The stated requirement is a bachelor degree, graduate diploma or postgraduate diploma in information technology, computer science or a related field. A marketing degree is not in a related IT field, so it does not directly meet the stated criteria; however, applications outside the criteria are assessed on a case-by-case basis.

question: What is the difference between the COMP803 and COMP806 internship options in the MIT?
gold_answer: COMP803 Internship is completed within two trimesters, whereas COMP806 Intensive Internship is completed within one trimester.

question: What is the total 2026 cost for an international MIT student including the Student Services Fee, and what does that fee pay for?
gold_answer: International 2026 fees total NZ$42,480 (NZ$38,940 programme fees plus NZ$3,540 resource fees), plus the compulsory Student Services Fee of NZ$300 per year. The SSF covers campus services such as counselling and pastoral care, careers guidance, sports and cultural activities, student associations, financial advice and health services.

question: In the MIT, which courses form the research pathway and the applied pathway at Level 9, and how many Level 9 credits are required?
gold_answer: The Level 9 component comprises 90 credits: the research option is COMP901 Information Technology Research Thesis, and the applied option is COMP902 Advanced Information Technology Specialised Project together with COMP903 Information Technology Applied Research Project.

question: How much is the AIS Student Services Fee and how is it charged?
gold_answer: The Student Services Fee is charged at NZ$300.00 per year, or NZ$30.00 per month or part thereof.

question: What proportion of the Student Services Fee is allocated to counselling and pastoral care?
gold_answer: 52% of the SSF is allocated to counselling services and pastoral care, including student orientation, student support and the employee assistance programme.

question: How often does the Student/Management Forum meet, and who sits on it?
gold_answer: The Student/Management Forum meets once a trimester and comprises student representatives from each programme. It provides input on non-academic matters, including consultation on the Student Services Fee.

question: If my enrolment lasts 14 months, how is the Student Services Fee charged for the two months beyond the first year?
gold_answer: The SSF is NZ$300 per year, or NZ$30 per month or part thereof. After the first year (NZ$300), the additional two months are charged at NZ$30 each, i.e. NZ$60, giving NZ$360 in total for 14 months.

question: What GPA is required for a certificate of Excellence in bachelor degree studies at AIS?
gold_answer: A certificate of Excellence requires a GPA of 7.5 and above, calculated on all course grades for the current programme in the prior one to two trimesters totalling not less than 60 credits and not previously counted for an award.

question: What academic award can an MIT student earn for their first block of Level 8 credits?
gold_answer: A Certificate of Academic Excellence in Postgraduate Studies is awarded for a GPA of 6.5 or above for the first block of credits, which for the MIT is 90 Level 8 credits.

question: How often is the Recognition of Academic Achievement ceremony held at AIS?
gold_answer: The Recognition of Academic Achievement ceremony is held each trimester for the presentation of awards.

question: My GPA over my last 60 bachelor-degree credits is 7.0. Which achievement award do I qualify for?
gold_answer: A GPA of 7.0 meets the minimum of 6.5 for a certificate of Merit but is below the 7.5 needed for Excellence, so you would qualify for the certificate of Merit (provided the credits are from the prior one to two trimesters and not previously counted).

question: Credits from my last two trimesters were already counted for a Merit award. Can the same credits count towards another achievement award?
gold_answer: No. The GPA for an award is calculated on credits not previously counted for an award, so the same credits cannot be counted again.

question: For the MIT, how many Level 8 credits form the first award block for the postgraduate excellence certificate, and what does that Level 8 component consist of?
gold_answer: For the MIT the first award block is 90 Level 8 credits (GPA 6.5 or above earns the Certificate of Academic Excellence in Postgraduate Studies). The Level 8 component comprises 90 credits of Level 8 IT courses, including the compulsory COMP801 Research Methods.

question: What does the AIS Scholarship cover, and who is eligible to apply?
gold_answer: The AIS Scholarship pays 50% of the tuition fee for the first year of study in any Diploma, Bachelor degree, Graduate Diploma, Postgraduate Diploma or Master programme, including the MBA and MIT. It is available to domestic students and awarded on a combination of academic merit and financial need.

question: When do AIS Scholarship applications close, and when are successful applicants notified?
gold_answer: Applications close four weeks before the start of the intended semester, and successful applicants are notified two weeks before the semester starts. Applications received after the advertised closing date are not considered.

question: What is the Women in Information Technology Scholarship worth?
gold_answer: It pays 50% of the tuition fee for the first year of study in any AIS Information Technology programme, including the MIT, and can save recipients more than $8,500.

question: What are the eligibility criteria for a Chairman's Scholarship at AIS?
gold_answer: Applicants must be a citizen or permanent resident of New Zealand, the Cook Islands, Tokelau, Niue or Australia; be nominated by a secondary school; be aged 17 or over; meet the entry requirements of the level at which they are nominated; and demonstrate school and community participation, with references from both school and community.

question: I am an international student on a student visa. Can I apply for the AIS Scholarship?
gold_answer: No. AIS scholarships, including the AIS Scholarship, are available to domestic students, so an international student on a student visa is not eligible.

question: Can I still apply for the AIS Scholarship two weeks before the semester starts?
gold_answer: No. Applications close four weeks before the start of the intended semester and applications received after the advertised closing date are not considered, so an application two weeks before the semester would be too late.

question: If a domestic student wins the Women in IT Scholarship for the MIT, how does it relate to the 2026 domestic programme fee?
gold_answer: The scholarship pays 50% of the tuition fee for the first year of study in an AIS IT programme including the MIT. The 2026 domestic MIT programme fee is NZ$9,720 (plus NZ$3,540 resource fees), so the scholarship halves the first-year tuition component of that cost.

question: Which cloud computing courses are available in the BIT Computer Networks specialisation and the PGDIT Networks and Security topic?

question: Which 2026 trimester dates apply to BIT students, and how long does the whole BIT take?

question: I will finish my MIT in August 2026. Am I eligible for the 2026 graduation ceremony, and by when must I apply?

question: What help does AIS offer for finding internships, and which BIT elective provides industry practice?
gold_answer: The Student Support Centre helps students find internships and employment through CV and cover letter preparation, job search advice, interview preparation and employability workshops; within the BIT, COMP722 Information Technology Industry Practice is an elective providing industry practice.

question: What share of the Student Services Fee funds careers guidance, and which AIS unit delivers that service?
gold_answer: 18% of the Student Services Fee is allocated to employment and careers information, advice and guidance; the Student Support Centre delivers these services, including CV help, job search advice, interview preparation and employability workshops.

question: I hold a relevant New Zealand Level 5 diploma. How much advanced standing can I get towards the BIT, and how many credits does the BIT require in total?
gold_answer: You may be entitled to advanced standing credit of up to 240 credits when entering a bachelor degree; the BIT requires 360 credits in total, so at least 120 credits would still need to be completed at AIS.

question: Which AIS IT qualifications sit at Level 7, and how do their credit totals differ?
gold_answer: Two AIS IT qualifications are at Level 7: the Bachelor of Information Technology (360 credits, 36 months) and the Graduate Diploma in Information Technology (135 credits, 12 months).

question: As an international NZDITTS student, what English level do I need for entry, and what attendance must I maintain for visa renewal?
gold_answer: Entry to the NZDITTS requires English equivalent to IELTS 5.5 (Academic) with no band less than 5.0; once studying, international students must maintain over 95% attendance and pass at least 75% of courses for a student visa renewal.

question: What is the difference in total 2025 international fees between the GDIT and the PGDIT?
gold_answer: For international students in 2025, the GDIT totals NZ$26,532 (NZ$23,967 plus NZ$2,565 resource fees) and the PGDIT totals NZ$27,040 (NZ$24,760 plus NZ$2,280 resource fees) - a difference of NZ$508.

question: Which courses appear in both the BIT Software Development specialisation and the GDIT Software Development specialist topic?
gold_answer: SOFT605 Object Oriented Programming, SOFT606 Desktop Applications Development, SOFT703 Web Applications Development and SOFT708 Mobile Applications Development appear in both.

question: Do the MIT and the PGDIT have the same English language entry requirement?
gold_answer: Yes. Both require IELTS 6.5 with no band lower than 6.0, TOEFL iBT 79 with a writing score of 21, PToE academic 58 with no band lower than 50, or NZCEL (Academic) Level 5.

question: What internship options exist in the PGDIT and in the MIT, and how long does each take?
gold_answer: In the PGDIT, COMP803 Internship runs 15 hours a week for 26 weeks (390 hours), COMP804 Industrial Project is a two-trimester supervised industry project, and COMP806 Intensive Internship takes one trimester. In the MIT, COMP803 Internship is completed within two trimesters and COMP806 Intensive Internship within one trimester.

question: I want to study artificial intelligence. Which course covers it in the PGDIT and in the MIT?
gold_answer: INFO813 Artificial Intelligence: it is one of the Information Systems specialist courses in both the PGDIT and the MIT.

question: Before writing my COMP901 thesis, where can I consult previous AIS theses, and what word count is expected?
gold_answer: The AIS Library's Theses Room Collection at St Helens Campus holds more than 1,500 MBA and MIT theses; the COMP901 thesis itself is expected to be between 30,000 and 50,000 words.

question: What computer equipment do BIT students receive, and what are the AIS BYOD minimum requirements?
gold_answer: All BIT students are issued with their own laptop and free Microsoft software. Under the AIS BYOD policy, devices must run iOS 13, Android 12 or Windows 11 in English, be Office 365 compatible, and have at least a 10-inch screen, 8GB memory (16GB preferred), Wi-Fi, mouse/keyboard or touchscreen, webcam, microphone and speakers.

question: How much Student Services Fee would I pay over the full 16-month MIT?
gold_answer: The SSF is NZ$300 per year or NZ$30 per month or part thereof. The MIT takes 16 months, so the SSF would be NZ$300 for the first year plus NZ$30 for each of the four additional months - NZ$420 in total.

question: My overall IELTS score is 6.0. Can I be admitted to the PGDIT?
gold_answer: No. The PGDIT requires IELTS 6.5 with no individual band lower than 6.0, so an overall 6.0 does not meet the requirement.

question: I am 16 years old and have the required NCEA credits. Can I enrol in the BIT?
gold_answer: No. BIT entrants must be 17 years or over, so you would need to wait until you turn 17.

question: I hold a bachelor's degree in marketing. Can I enter the Graduate Diploma in Information Technology?
gold_answer: Yes. The GDIT requires a bachelor degree at least equivalent to New Zealand pass standard and does not restrict the subject, so a marketing degree meets the academic requirement (subject to the English requirement).

question: I hold a bachelor's degree in marketing. Can I enter the Postgraduate Diploma in Information Technology?
gold_answer: No. The PGDIT requires a Bachelor's degree or Graduate Diploma in Information Technology, Computer Science or a related field, so a marketing degree does not meet the stated criteria.

question: My TOEFL iBT total is 60 but my writing score is 17. Do I meet the BIT English requirement through TOEFL?
gold_answer: No. The BIT TOEFL pathway requires iBT 60 with a writing score of 18, so a writing score of 17 falls short; another accepted qualification would be needed.

question: I completed my qualification in October 2025. Am I eligible to attend the 2026 graduation ceremony?
gold_answer: Yes. All students who complete a Level 5 or above qualification between October 2025 and early September 2026 inclusive are eligible to attend the 2026 ceremony.

question: I expect to finish my programme in late September 2026. Can I attend the 2026 graduation ceremony?
gold_answer: No. Only students who complete a Level 5 or above qualification between October 2025 and early September 2026 inclusive are eligible for the 2026 ceremony, so completion in late September 2026 falls outside the window. If an application has been made and the qualification is not completed in time, it is withdrawn and any graduation fees paid are refunded.

question: My final results are not out yet. Should I wait before applying to graduate at the 2026 ceremony?
gold_answer: No, don't wait. Submit the Application to Graduate as early as possible because applications are not accepted after the deadline; if you do not complete in time, the application is withdrawn and any graduation fees paid are refunded.

question: I still have unpaid fines at AIS. Can I formally graduate at the ceremony?
gold_answer: Not until they are cleared. To formally graduate you must have paid all outstanding fees and/or fines and completed a Student Clearance Form.

question: Can I replace one of my PGDIT specialist courses with COMP805 Specialisation Project?
gold_answer: Yes. Some PGDIT courses can be replaced with COMP805 Specialisation Project or COMP722 Information Technology Industry Practice, with approval from the Academic Head of Programme.

question: As a BIT student, can I take a course from outside the Information Technology programme?
gold_answer: Possibly. The inclusion of courses outside the Information Technology programme may be considered with the approval of the Academic Head of Programme.

question: I have no tertiary qualifications. Can I start the NZ Diploma in IT Technical Support?
gold_answer: Yes. No previous tertiary qualifications are necessary for the NZDITTS, but you need 40 credits at NCEA Level 2 or above (including at least 10 literacy and 10 numeracy credits) and English equivalent to IELTS 5.5 with no band below 5.0.

question: If I complete the NZDITTS and then enrol in the BIT, can my diploma study count towards the degree?
gold_answer: Yes. Cross-credits for subsequent IT study are available after the NZDIT Technical Support, and a student entering a bachelor's degree with a completed relevant New Zealand Level 5-6 qualification may be entitled to advanced standing credit of up to 240 credits (identified on application; no application or fee; subject to Board of Studies approval).

question: My PToE academic score is 58 with no band below 50. Do I meet the PGDIT English requirement?
gold_answer: Yes. The PGDIT accepts a PToE academic score of 58 with no band lower than 50, so your score exactly meets the requirement.

question: I chose the PGDIT research pathway. Which course must I take in my first trimester?
gold_answer: COMP801 Research Methods must be taken in your first trimester if you follow the COMP802 Research Project pathway.

question: I want to finish my PGDIT internship within a single trimester. Which option should I choose?
gold_answer: COMP806 Intensive Internship, which is completed over one trimester.

question: I can only attend classes on weekends. Which AIS programmes run weekend classes in 2026?
gold_answer: The MBA and PGDBA run weekend classes: in 2026 they run every weekend from 31 January to 18 December.

question: If I have not paid the academic dress hireage fee by the deadline, can I still attend the 2026 graduation ceremony?
gold_answer: No. Both the application and payment of the academic dress hireage fee are due by 5.00pm on Friday 11 September, and applications are not accepted after the deadline.

question: I am an international student. Can I apply for a Chairman's Scholarship?
gold_answer: No. Chairman's Scholarships require citizenship or permanent residency of New Zealand, the Cook Islands, Tokelau, Niue or Australia, plus nomination by a secondary school, so an international student is not eligible.
